ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders holding 25% or more, and trade counterparties against: (1) FINTRAC PCMLTFA-defined politically exposed persons (PEP) categories, including domestic and foreign PEPs and their close associates; (2) Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (3) the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, given the use of USD/EUR correspondent banking rails; (4) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; and (5) provincial AML/CFT compliance directives. Enhanced due diligence, beneficial ownership verification, and Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) filing obligations apply upon any PEP, sanctions, adverse media, or high-risk jurisdiction indicator.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - official online corporate searches and NUANS name clearance module, accessible directly or through authorized registry agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Business Corporations Act and applicable naming regulations, a corporate name may be in English, French, or a combination of both; all names must use Latin-alphabet letters and Arabic numerals, with accents permitted for French. Names originating in non-Latin scripts must provide a duly transliterated phonetic version using recognized romanization. The proposed name must be distinguishable from all existing corporate, limited partnership, business, and registered trademark names in the NUANS database, and must not suggest a connection with a Crown body, public office, or regulated profession absent express consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director of Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, rejects a proposed corporate name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request to the Director within 30 days of the rejection notice. The request must include the NUANS report, a detailed explanation of the distinctive elements of the proposed name, consent or letters from affected parties, and any corrective trademark clearance evidence. The Director's review decision may then be challenged by judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Business Corporations Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, s. 3, with service on the Director and preservation of all original filing fees.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a standard low-risk wholesale trading corporation in Alberta, provided the registered office is a genuine physical street address in Alberta (not a post office box), service of process can be accepted at that address, and the provider is a licensed corporate registry agent or registered office provider. Banks and trade finance lenders may, however, require an additional physical presence or director meeting location under their own AML/KYC and commercial substance policies.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5%-10%) for a non-licensed ISIC 4638 dehydrated vegetables and spices wholesale trading entity with no FINTRAC reporting obligation. The risk rises to 10%-15% if the entity later becomes a FINTRAC-reporting entity, holds an agricultural or food safety licence, or uses shared commercial premises that attract CRA or CFIA verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 5-16, 101-114
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta / Alberta Registries
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under the Alberta Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. A standard commercial corporation may be incorporated without initial paid-up capital, and shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine. No escrow account or mandatory capital deposit applies to a general trading corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the initial subscriptions for common shares of the Corporation be and are hereby accepted, and that 100 common shares be issued to the subscribers as shown in the subscription register. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the address of the registered office of the Corporation be established at [Insert Registered Office Address], in the City of [City], Alberta, and that the corporate registers and minute books be maintained at that address. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT [Name] be appointed as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each to act until successors are duly appointed. AND FURTHER RESOLVED that any director or officer be authorized to execute all instruments ancillary to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Online Corporate Name Search Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search in the Alberta Corporate Registry database to confirm the proposed name is distinctive and not confusingly similar. Submit a Name Reservation Request through the Corporate Registry online portal; the reservation remains valid for 90 days. Alternatively, the company may proceed directly with a numerical name by filing Articles of Incorporation without a name reservation.
required_dossiers: Name Search Report or Name Reservation Request receipt
Third-party consent, if distinctive name is requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or objected to, file a revised Name Reservation Request or abandon the proposed name and proceed using a Registry-assigned numerical corporate name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Registration Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute Articles of Incorporation in Form 1, stating the registered office city, share structure, maximum number of shares, restrictions on share transfers, and the names and residence addresses of the first directors. Ensure at least one director satisfies applicable Alberta resident Canadian director requirements. Submit the executed articles online or by paper, pay the prescribed filing fee, and retain the filing receipt.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) signed by each incorporator
Name reservation receipt or numerical name election
Registered office address and first director list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a Notice of Deficiency, correct and resubmit the deficient documents within the stated cure period. If the application is rejected, amend the Articles and refile with a new filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation containing the unique Alberta corporate identification number. This certificate marks the commencement of corporate existence and should be retained in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation is not issued after the stated service standard, contact the Alberta Corporate Registry contact centre, confirm payment and submitted forms, and request expedited issuance or file a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Corporate Record-Keeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Set the registered office at a physical, full street address in Alberta as indicated in the Articles. A post office box without a physical address is not sufficient. Establish the corporate minute book containing registers of directors, shareholders, transfers, other securities, and corporate records. Adopt by-laws and, if desired, a corporate seal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office is found to be invalid or incomplete, file a Notice of Change of Registered Office with Alberta Corporate Registry and ensure continuous maintenance of statutory records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Board Resolution, Officer Appointment, and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the initial board meeting or obtain unanimous written consents. Adopt the first board resolution approving share subscriptions, establishing the registered office, and appointing officers. Issue share certificates to subscribers and record all issuances in the share register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a share issuance is challenged for lack of authorization, ratify by subsequent shareholder resolution or, where necessary, return and reissue shares under a corrected board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Alberta Municipal and Food Safety Authorities, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the Canada Revenue Agency for a Business Number, corporation income tax account, GST/HST account where required, payroll account if employees are hired, and an import/export account if applicable. If food commodities are physically exported or processed, assess whether a Safe Food for Canadians Act licence is required.
required_dossiers: CRA registration forms (e.g., RC1 or online Business Registration)
Safe Food for Canadians Act licence application, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is rejected or queried, correct the legal name, incorporation number, or registered office details in CRA My Business Account and resubmit the affected registration forms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no Alberta industrial or manufacturing licence is required for dehydrated-spice wholesale trading under ISIC 4638. If physical premises are occupied, municipal licensing and Alberta occupational safety authorities become relevant.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate provincial industrial operating permit applies to a pure dehydrated-spice trading business. The company must comply with ordinary municipal business licensing and, where applicable, Canadian Food Inspection Agency food export requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no environmental impact assessment is triggered for wholesale warehousing and trading. If the company later adds dehydration, grinding, or wastewater-producing processing, a screening assessment may apply under Alberta's Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No material wastewater or VOC emissions are expected from warehousing and spice trading. If cleaning, refrigeration, or ventilation systems are installed, comply with municipal sewer bylaws, Alberta ventilation emission limits, and Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 standards, including ozone-depleting substance handling rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code, structural occupancy inspection, and municipal building safety clearance must be obtained for any leased office or warehouse. Occupational Health and Safety registration and workplace hazard clearance are required before staffing the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; federal administrator of GST/HST, corporate income tax, and customs program accounts; digital portal: My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE via www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. Alberta does not levy a provincial sales tax or administer provincial corporate income tax; provincial tax is filed through the CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act. Alberta corporate registry matters are handled by Service Alberta / Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) or Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA) and obtain the Alberta corporate registry file number. Step 2: Apply to the CRA for the 15-digit statutory Business Number (BN) online, by telephone, or by filing Form RC1 Request for a Business Number. Step 3: Activate program accounts under the BN: RT for GST/HST, RC for federal corporate income tax, and RP for payroll where applicable; obtain an RM customs importer/exporter program account through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). Step 4: Where the corporation is controlled by non-residents, designate a Canadian representative and comply with any forms required by the CRA for non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada. Step 5: Register on the CBSA CARM portal (CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management) to transmit commercial export declarations and e-manifests electronically. Step 6: No separate Alberta provincial tax ID is required; the federal BN and program accounts constitute the complete statutory tax identity for GST and income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A CBCA/ABCA Business Corporation is a Canadian-resident corporation subject to federal and Alberta corporate income tax under Income Tax Act Part I and the Alberta Corporate Tax Act; no pass-through or check-the-box classification is available. Canadian-resident corporations are taxed at the entity level on worldwide income, while non-resident shareholders are not subject to entity-level Canadian tax on dividends. Alberta applies a flat provincial corporate rate with no provincial capital tax and no provincial sales tax, but the entity remains an exclusive GST/HST registrant rather than a flow-through vehicle.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists for CBCA/ABCA corporations; entity-level taxation is mandatory. Material elections available to an export trader include: (a) voluntary GST/HST registration under Excise Tax Act s. 240(3) for exporters of zero-rated goods to claim input tax credits even below the CAD 30,000 threshold; (b) joint election under ETA s. 156 for closely related corporations to treat intercompany taxable supplies as made by a single registrant; (c) non-calendar fiscal period election under ITA s. 11; (d) associated-corporation allocation election under ITA s. 256 for income attribution. Hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.2 to 18.7 are mandatory and are not subject to taxpayer election, consistent with OECD BEPS Action 2.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) regime under the Excise Tax Act, administered by the CRA. Alberta applies the federal 5% GST only; there is no provincial sales tax (PST) or HST component in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold under ETA s. 123(1) and s. 148; mandatory registration under ETA s. 240(1) once exceeded). Zero-rated export supplies count toward the threshold, so a bulk dehydrated spice exporter must register even if all customers are non-residents. Voluntary registration under ETA s. 240(3) is available below the threshold to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, biometric invoicing, or government-API pre-approval requirement. Registered suppliers must issue and retain invoices satisfying ETA s. 220 to s. 224 and the Input Tax Information Regulations, including supplier name, Business Number, invoice date, description, and zero-rating status; CRA accepts PDF, XML, EDI, and other electronic formats in English or French. Pan-Canadian Peppol BIS electronic invoicing is voluntary under the Digital Interchange Canada pilot and not yet mandatory. For exports, the binding mandatory electronic filing is the CBSA CARM portal, which requires approved customs partners to transmit B-13 export declarations, e-manifests, and cargo-level data electronically before or at departure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 1 (supply of tangible personal property sold for export) and s. 2 (supply to a non-resident person for subsequent export). Bulk dehydrated garlic flakes (HS 0712.90) and crushed chili pepper (HS 0904.21/0904.22) qualify where: (i) the supplier is a GST/HST registrant; (ii) possession of the goods transfers to a non-resident purchaser in Canada; (iii) the goods are exported as part of the supply within 60 days after delivery without substantial use or alteration in Canada; (iv) the supplier retains documentary proof of export (customs declaration, bill of lading, commercial invoice, payment evidence); and (v) the transaction is made on commercial terms (Incoterms FOB, CIF, or EXW) transferring risk and title to the foreign buyer. International freight services directly linked to the exported goods are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part VII. Refunds are secured by claiming input tax credits in the exporter's GST/HST return; a net refund arises where zero-rated exports exceed taxable purchases.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Customs Export Declaration (B-13/A8A or A8A/B1) transmitted through the CARM commercial portal
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing direct shipment to the non-resident purchaser
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or TT bank credit advice confirming foreign currency settlement
Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and Certificate of Origin referencing HS 0712.90 or HS 0904 classification
Executed export contract and proof of non-resident purchaser status (purchase order, Incoterms, foreign registry data)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and CBSA Export Verification Unit may audit export substantiation for up to seven years (ETA s. 298(1); the normal four-year reassessment period is extended to seven years for misrepresentation and is unlimited in fraud cases). Where the required customs documentation bundle is incomplete or inconsistent, CRA reassesses the supply at 5% GST, disallows associated input tax credits retroactively, and imposes civil penalties: ETA s. 280 failure-to-file penalty of 5% plus 1% per month; ETA s. 285 gross negligence penalty of 25% of the understated net tax; and compound interest under ETA s. 280. Fraudulent export zero-rating schemes involving false bills of lading, recycled customs declarations, or fictitious non-resident buyers trigger criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327.07 and ITA s. 239, with fines up to 200% of the evaded amount, imprisonment, and permanent denial of the exporter's GST/HST refund entitlement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority. Statutory foreign-exchange administration is distributed across the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential supervision, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF reporting, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for export declarations, the Department of Finance Canada for Investment Canada Act administration, and Payments Canada (PayNet) for clearing and settlement. Canada maintains no statutory exchange-control commission; exchange controls were repealed in 1951.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full Canadian-dollar convertibility on both current and capital account. No Bank of Canada licence, FX permit, or approval is required for conversion or cross-border remittance of funds. Profit remittances (dividends, interest, royalties, branch profits) are unrestricted at the monetary level and are subject only to: (i) Part XIII withholding tax of 25% with treaty reductions, for example 5% for a substantial corporate holder under the Canada-United States treaty; (ii) FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting for transactions of CAD 10,000 or more; and (iii) the remitting bank's KYC/EDD assessment of underlying commercial documentation. Practical constraint is bank validation of the trade contract and corporate resolution; no currency-quota or conversion-ticket obstacles exist.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no surrender mandate, no mandatory CAD conversion ratio, no retention ceiling, and no repatriation window on foreign-currency export proceeds. Exporters may hold proceeds indefinitely in USD or other permitted foreign accounts. Statutory obligations: (i) CBSA export declaration form B13A filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED) for all shipments valued at CAD 2,000 or more and for controlled goods regardless of value; (ii) FINTRAC EFT reports for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; (iii) Statistics Canada international merchandise-trade reporting; and (iv) Canadian corporate income-tax recognition of foreign-exchange gains and losses per the Income Tax Act functional-currency rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act, ABA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each incorporation or amalgamation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late filing fee after 2-month deadline; continued non-filing for approximately 1 year may result in administrative strike-off and subsequent dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal; includes Alberta corporate income tax administered by CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; daily compound interest; possible director liability for withheld amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required for distributing corporations and those offering shares to the public; non-distributing private corporations may waive the audit by unanimous shareholder consent under section 190 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II); financial statements must be prepared in accordance with applicable generally accepted accounting principles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta has no provincial UBO annual filing. Share transfers must be reported by the registered shareholder to the corporation, and the register of members must be updated within a reasonable time; annual shareholder meeting minutes must confirm transfers and changes in shareholdings. The register of members is evidentiary proof of share ownership.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 185 - 600 (typical Alberta registered agent and office services range: CAD 250 - 800 per year)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 if audit waived by unanimous consent; otherwise approximately 3,700 - 11,000 for a small exporting private corporation (CAD 5,000 - 15,000).

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate income tax rate (federal 15% plus Alberta provincial 8%).
